claims.assertion: Ley 11/2023 Title I transposes the EAA for listed products and consumer services.

sources.evidence: Lists covered consumer products and services, including computing, terminals, e-readers, communications, audiovisual access, passenger transport elements, banking, e-books and e-commerce.

claims.review_note: Current consolidated BOE opened on 2026-09-24. EAA context; not the WAD. Link reachable at BOE.

claims.assertion: The existing Yes means a dedicated public EAA accessibility-statement page is required on a company's website.

sources.evidence: Requires conformity information in general terms or equivalent and public written/oral accessible availability, without expressly naming a dedicated website statement page.

claims.review_note: Existing ✔️ Yes preserved with explicit EAA-specific source-needed qualification. In user-supplied 'Questions about reporting for the EAA (8).eml', the 24 September 2026 outgoing message asks UTAC whether a company website must publish a public accessibility statement; no response to that question appears. The existing row refers to arts. 7–9, which concern product-side requirements rather than proof of a dedicated service page. Before-merge manual research task; do not infer No.

claims.assertion: Providers include information assessing how the service meets accessibility requirements in their general terms or equivalent document.

sources.evidence: Requires information assessing how the service meets Art. 3 requirements in general terms or equivalent document.

claims.review_note: Separate isolated Spanish-to-English language review on 2026-09-24: correction applied to retain 'assessing how' and Art. 3; final English wording rechecked against literal rendering. Original excerpt 'incluirán, en las condiciones generales o documento equivalente, la información que evalúe de qué manera el servicio cumple...' Literal: include in general terms or equivalent information assessing how the service meets requirements. Initial shortened wording needed correction; final claim preserves assessment of how.

claims.assertion: The Art. 13 information is publicly available in written and oral form and accessible to persons with disabilities.

sources.evidence: Requires information available to public in written and oral formats and accessibly for persons with disabilities, maintained current while service operates.

claims.review_note: This is a public availability obligation; it does not by itself prove a separate statement page.

claims.assertion: The public may request information separately from the required publicly available Art. 13 information.

sources.evidence: Public availability established; separate on-request mode not expressly established in these provisions.

claims.review_note: Do not conflate public availability with a separate public-on-request duty.

claims.assertion: Providers furnish all information necessary to demonstrate service conformity on a reasoned competent-authority request.

sources.evidence: Reasoned authority request triggers provision of all information needed to demonstrate conformity.

claims.review_note: Isolated language review corrected the shortened wording to retain 'all information necessary' and reasoned request. Original excerpt 'Sobre la base de una solicitud motivada ... toda la información necesaria...' Literal: on a reasoned request, all necessary information. Final claim supported after correction.

claims.assertion: Autonomous communities and Ceuta/Melilla determine surveillance authorities within their competences; other authorities' powers under supplementary regulations remain possible.

sources.evidence: Regional/autonomous city designation and caveat for other regulatory powers.

claims.review_note: Statutory authority class rather than an exhaustive current named roster. Isolated Spanish review supported wording with 'determine' and powers caveat. Existing UTAC-only display misleadingly suggested it was sole surveillance body. Individual regional designations were not verified within this pass. Language agent final wording check: 'retain powers' was rejected; use 'may have powers' to preserve conditional pudiera tener. Table omits supplementary-powers detail for brevity.
claims.scope: Products, E-commerce, Banking, Electronic communications, Transport, Audiovisual access, E-books

claims.assertion: UTAC coordinates and supports surveillance authorities and serves as an information contact for citizens and economic operators.

sources.evidence: Directorate-General assumes technical unit; advisory, coordination and contact functions.
Government page describes coordination and public contact.

claims.review_note: UTAC government link opened to correct agency. It is not the universal designated regional supervisor. Isolated agent found coordination/support not established by the supplied art. 3(g),(h) excerpts alone; art. 3(a) and official UTAC page explicitly supply that role.

claims.assertion: UTAC acts as the surveillance authority in areas where none has been designated.

sources.evidence: Express fallback surveillance authority where no authority designated.

claims.review_note: Isolated language review supported this precise conditional wording. Does not prove that a particular region/sector is currently undesignated. Language agent final verdict Supported: 'acts as surveillance authority where none has been designated.'

claims.assertion: Individual designated authorities are named and verified for each region and product/service sector.

sources.evidence: Designations are to be determined by autonomous communities and Ceuta/Melilla and notified to UTAC.

claims.review_note: No verified complete current public roster found in bounded research. Keep statutory class and coordination body; do not claim named regional coverage.

claims.assertion: A named authority is established for accessibility of 112 emergency-call answering.

sources.evidence: Sets accessibility requirements for response to 112 communications.

claims.review_note: The specific answering-centre oversight body and reporting route were not verified; separate from electronic-communications providers.

claims.assertion: The public can send Ley 11/2023 accessibility noncompliance reports or complaints to UTAC by email.

sources.evidence: Government page expressly instructs those wishing to report or complain of Ley 11/2023 accessibility failures to email utac@dsca.gob.es with case description.
Technical unit provides suitable means to receive reports and complaints on Title I compliance.

claims.review_note: Published UTAC page opened and identified the precise EAA purpose; email has no login prerequisite. UTAC coordinates and may direct matters within its remit; this is not proof it is the final local deciding authority. Language agent final verdict Supported for 'Public complaints and reports' and instruction to describe the Ley 11/2023 case.

reporting_route.sector: Ley 11/2023 Title I products and services

claims.assertion: Companies may send reports to UTAC's contact email if within UTAC's competence.

sources.evidence: Publishes utac@dsca.gob.es for Ley 11/2023 noncompliance reports; company-specific acceptance independently supplied in official correspondence.
Contact point expressly includes economic operators.

claims.review_note: Official UTAC reply dated 20 Aug 2026 in user-supplied EML explicitly says companies can also email UTAC if within its competence; no state-level company-specific tool. Preserve exact limitation. Generic reports are established, but dedicated Art. 13(7) non-compliance and Art. 16(7) exemption filing at a particular regional authority are not. No message was sent by this audit.

reporting_route.sector: Ley 11/2023 Title I within UTAC competence

claims.assertion: A specific state-level company reporting tool exists.

sources.evidence: Mandates appropriate means for contact/complaints, does not identify dedicated company portal.

claims.review_note: 20 Aug 2026 UTAC reply says no specific state-level company reporting tool was available then. Time-specific official correspondence; not an assertion that regional tools do not exist.

claims.assertion: Companies outside Spain may report to UTAC in English or French under the stated language condition.

sources.evidence: Economic operators are within UTAC contact role; language acceptance is evidenced only by the dated UTAC reply.

claims.review_note: 20 Aug 2026 UTAC official reply in user-supplied EML: companies outside Spain can report in English or French if they do not speak Spanish or the relevant co-official language. This concerns UTAC contact, not all regional authorities. Correspondence content is summarized, not publicly reproduced.
claims.scope: UTAC reports from companies outside Spain

reporting_route.sector: Ley 11/2023 Title I within UTAC competence

claims.assertion: Covered service providers notify competent national authorities immediately when their service is noncompliant.

sources.evidence: Immediate notice to competent national authorities in Member States where service provided, with noncompliance and corrective measures.

claims.review_note: Duty established, but exact regional destination and intake route for this statutory notice remain Unknown. Isolated language review corrected territorial scope.

claims.assertion: Agents invoking fundamental alteration or disproportionate burden send information to the relevant surveillance/service verification authority, except microenterprises.

sources.evidence: Exceptional alteration/burden grounds; information to relevant authorities when invoked; paragraph 7 not applicable to microenterprises.

claims.review_note: EAA Article 14 context; obligation does not establish an email/form for regional exemption submission.
claims.scope: Covered products and services, excluding microenterprises from notification

claims.assertion: A verified purpose-specific destination for company non-compliance notices to each designated authority is identified.

sources.evidence: Requires notification but does not supply route.

claims.review_note: UTAC general company reports are not presumed to discharge formal notifications to other competent authorities.

claims.assertion: A verified company exemption-notification channel for each designated authority is identified.

sources.evidence: Requires information to relevant authorities, with microenterprise exception, but no channel.

claims.review_note: Follow-up needed; do not relabel UTAC generic reports as formal exemption filing.

claims.assertion: UTAC reply of 20 Aug 2026 confirmed regional designation, a state-level contact email usable by companies within its competence, conditional English/French reporting and absence of a dedicated state tool at that time.

sources.evidence: Official statutory role and 2026 establishment, used to corroborate institution; details of reply derive from private official correspondence.
